expected_claims.text: The answer identifies the current stable Kubernetes release as of the answer date and cites official Kubernetes release evidence.

evidence.required_locator: official Kubernetes release page, changelog, or release notes
evidence.must_support: current stable version and release date

expected_claims.text: The answer identifies the current stable Docker Engine release as of the answer date and cites official Docker release evidence.

evidence.must_support: current stable version and release date

expected_claims.text: The upgrade plan checks compatibility risks for Kubernetes API removals or deprecations, container runtime behavior, networking, storage, and supported version skew.

evidence.required_locator: Kubernetes version-skew, deprecation, or upgrade documentation
evidence.must_support: API, component, or version compatibility constraints

evidence.required_locator: Docker Engine upgrade or compatibility documentation
evidence.must_support: engine upgrade risks or compatibility notes

unsupported_if: The answer provides version numbers without an explicit answer date.
The answer uses unofficial mirrors or stale third-party summaries when official release notes are available.
The answer treats the latest version as safe to deploy without checking compatibility and deprecation evidence.
